thread:
mika: Heads-up — we're seeing a token mix shift from the new 'contextual search' feature. Avg ctx went from ~1.2k to ~5.5k tokens and streaming calls jumped to ~68% of requests. Need quick capacity/forecast sanity check before the spring campaign.

samir: Oof. Do we have new TPS or total monthly tokens numbers?

mika: Traffic volume same (requests/sec ~ 120), but avg tokens/request up ~4.5x. So monthly token consumption projected up ~4x.

julia: Quick back-of-envelope: if per-GPU sustained generation throughput (streaming workload, mixed batch) ~450 tps at that context profile, and requests are 120 rps * 60s * 60 * 24 * 30 ~ 10.4M req/mo, avg tokens/request 5.5k -> monthly_tokens ~5.7e10.

liam: Can you paste that calc? I want GPU-hours to budget.

julia: Sure. Rough snippet:
```
monthly_reqs = 120 * 3600 * 24 * 30  # ~10.4M
avg_tokens = 5500
monthly_tokens = monthly_reqs * avg_tokens  # ~5.7e10 tokens
gpu_tps = 450  # tokens/sec sustained (streaming-friendly)
gpu_seconds = monthly_tokens / gpu_tps
gpu_hours = gpu_seconds / 3600
# gpu_hours ≈ (5.7e10 / 450) / 3600 ≈ 35,000 GPU-hours/mo
```

samir: 35k GPU-hours/mo — that's 1.1k GPU-days -> if we want 24/7 steady capacity ~47 GPUs continuously. But we need headroom for spikes/rollouts. For a 2x safety margin -> ~94 GPUs reserved.

mika: Current dedicated pool in us-west-2 is 40 GPUs (reserved) + autoscale to 70 on burst. So we'd blow past burst.

liam: Two levers: 1) reduce per-token cost via caching/prefix reuse (we can cache long system prompts and some prefixes), 2) push more traffic to non-streaming (batch) endpoints for longer context inference where throughput is higher. Non-streaming batch throughput measured ~900 tps on same hardware for large contexts.

julia: If we can shift 30% of long-context work to batch endpoints, gpu_hours drops: with 30% at 900 tps and 70% at 450 tps => effective_tps = 0.3*900 + 0.7*450 = 585 tps -> gpu_hours ~ (monthly_tokens / 585) / 3600 ≈ 27k GPU-hours/mo. Good delta.

mika: Any networking/region constraints? A lot of this traffic is APAC — latency wants edge routing to ap-northeast. Do we have capacity there?

samir: ap-northeast-1 Dedicated pool is tiny (8 GPUs) and cold-start for burst adds ~5-7 min. We could route 60% of APAC to us-west with cross-region penalty but that increases p95 by ~120ms. For the campaign we could pre-warm a small portable pool in APAC (reserve an extra 24 GPUs for 72 hours) to handle peak. Cost vs latency trade-off.

liam: Ops-bot: queue length and GPU utilization for last 48h?
ops-bot: Recent 48h summary: avg GPU util 62%, p95 queue length 1.8s, streaming requests p95 latency +12% compared to non-streaming. Scheduled maintenance: none in next 7d.

julia: Also watch KV cache effectiveness — with longer contexts cache hit rate drops if prompt prefixes are more unique. We should run a quick eval to see hit rate before assuming caching savings.

samir: Actionables: 1) Ops: run a 72h pre-warm test in ap-northeast with 24 GPUs and measure p95 and autoscale stability (assigned to liam). 2) Product/devex: push a pilot to redirect 30% long-context to batch endpoints (assigned to julia). 3) Finance: prepare cost delta for +50 reserved GPUs in us-west and +24 in ap-northeast for 2 weeks (assigned to mika).

mika: I'll raise a PO request once numbers are in. Target timeline: tests start tomorrow, initial numbers by EOD+2.

liam: One more note — streaming has extra per-call overhead (more RPCs). For high-request-rate small-contexts streaming can reduce perf. We should throttle streaming to only long-context interactive flows.

julia: Agreed. I'll add a routing flag to the API to prefer batch when avg_ctx > 2k and let SDK default to batch for large uploads.

samir: Thanks. If test yields expected drop in GPU-hours we'll propose reserving 80-100 GPUs for the campaign and rely on burst for the rest. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:

mika: Thanks everyone. Will post results here.
